Current numerical weather prediction runs indicate a modest moderation from the colder-than-average conditions observed on August 6, consistent with the passage of a high-pressure ridge that reduces cloud cover and allows limited daytime warming. Official MetService guidance and ensemble outputs place the most likely daytime high in the 12–13°C range, with limited upside potential unless northerly advection strengthens.

The strong weighting toward 13°C reflects model consensus on these steering patterns and boundary-layer mixing, while the modest probabilities assigned to 12°C and 14°C capture remaining uncertainty in exact timing of frontal passages and local wind effects. Historical records show August maxima cluster tightly around 11–13°C, reinforcing why outcomes outside this narrow band carry low implied odds. Updated model runs and official briefings through August 7 morning will determine final resolution.
